summary: As of October 19, 2026, junk-bond spreads are 3.29 percentage points and are up 0.18 percentage points over five trading days. Investment-grade spreads are up 0.04 percentage points over those same five trading days. The CCC-minus-BB gap is 11.10 percentage points. Of the 0.09 percentage-point move in the all-in junk yield, 0.18 was the credit spread and 0.09 was Treasury rates. The 10-year yield is 5.15 percent as of October 19, 2026 and the 30-year is 5.48 percent as of October 19, 2026, a gap of 0.33 percentage points. Brent is 109.30 dollars a barrel as of October 20, 2026 (+3.42 percent over five trading days), and the curve is backwardation. The 5-year inflation breakeven is 2.39 percent as of October 20, 2026, up 0.06 percentage points over five observations. The 10-year real yield is 2.80 percent as of October 19, 2026. The broad dollar index is 121.40 as of October 16, 2026, +2.05 index points over 20 observations. VIX is 18.44 as of October 19, 2026. The Fed balance sheet is 6.76 trillion dollars as of October 14, 2026, up 9 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Reserve balances are 3.02 trillion dollars as of October 14, 2026, up 8 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Overnight reverse repo is 0.227 billion dollars as of October 20, 2026, up 0.026 billion over the latest four observations.
